puzzles.title: Volcanic Connections
puzzles.intro: Sixteen tiles, four hidden sets. Expect eruption-adjacent vocabulary, but not every word is there for the reason you think.
puzzles.trap: The main feint is that several words look purely volcanic at first glance, while one group actually hinges on common compounds and another on words that follow the same lead word.

puzzles.title: After Dark
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four hidden links. A few celestial-looking tiles are there to lure you into the wrong corners first.
puzzles.trap: The bait is night-sky vocabulary: some words look like they should form a straightforward astronomy set, but several actually belong to phrase-based groups like SHOOTING ___, ___ MOON, and things with RINGS.

puzzles.title: Coffee Break Confusion
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four groups. Some of the coffee-flavored surface links are real, and some are there to lead you astray.
puzzles.trap: I leaned on coffee-adjacent words like BEAN-type items, drink names, and cafe imagery so several tiles look like they belong together before the cleaner patterns emerge.

puzzles.title: Roll Camera
puzzles.intro: Sixteen film-flavored tiles hide four sets. Some look like they belong with movies in one way, but pair up better in another.
puzzles.trap: Several words tempt you toward obvious cinema buckets like genres or Oscar winners, while the real late-game twist is the phrase set built from common screen compounds.

puzzles.title: You Are Here
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four hidden groups. Since this one circles around maps, a few tiles may look like they belong somewhere more obvious at first glance.
puzzles.trap: The main feint is that several words lean geographic, but some of the trickiest ones are actually phrase-completion groups rather than map vocabulary.

puzzles.title: Dry Heat

groups.label: Words that become deserts when a letter is added

puzzles.intro: Sixteen words hide four sets. The theme points one way, but not every sandy-looking tile belongs where you first think.
puzzles.trap: Several entries look like straightforward desert vocabulary, but some are actually wordplay routes to dessert/desert via added or removed letters.

puzzles.title: Into the Woods
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words are tangled together here, with a leafy surface theme that won’t always help as much as it seems. Some belong deep in the forest; others only look like they do.
puzzles.trap: The big misdirection is that several words feel like they should make simple tree-or-forest sets, but some actually belong to phrase categories like BLACK ___ or ___ FOREST, and others hide in the much trickier “things with rings” group.

puzzles.title: Deep Space Static
puzzles.intro: Sixteen tiles, four hidden groups. Some of the most spacey-looking words are there to lure you away from the real connections.
puzzles.trap: Several words seem to belong in a straightforward astronomy set, but some actually work only through phrases like BLACK ___ or Cosmic ___.

puzzles.title: Tacking Points

groups.label: Nautical words that are also everyday verbs

puzzles.intro: Sixteen sailing-flavored words hide four groups. Some look like obvious boat terms, but a few are steering you somewhere else.
puzzles.trap: Several tiles seem to belong with generic boat parts or sailing actions, but some are actually there for wordplay like ___ KNOT and ___ SAIL.

puzzles.title: In the Frame
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four hidden groups. Since the theme is photography, expect some terms to look like they belong together before they actually do.
puzzles.trap: Several words read like generic camera actions or settings, but the main feint is that some photo-looking terms really work only through wordplay, especially the PHOTO- compounds.

puzzles.title: Storm Warning

groups.label: Hurricane categories on the Saffir–Simpson scale
Things represented by cloud symbols in weather forecasts

puzzles.intro: Sixteen weathery words, but the real patterns don’t all blow in from the same direction. Some apparent storm terms are only there to cloud the forecast.
puzzles.trap: I leaned on overlapping weather imagery: words like FIRE, SNOW, WIND, and LIGHTNING look like they should form a straightforward storm set, but they split across wordplay-based groups instead.

puzzles.title: Cold Cuts
puzzles.intro: A chilly grid with some very tempting overlaps. Don’t stop at the first cold-looking set you see.
puzzles.trap: Several words point toward ice, mountains, or frozen treats, so the glacier vocabulary is meant to blur with the age phrases and the snack words before the last set clicks.

puzzles.title: Woven In
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four hidden sets. Some of the textile-looking ones are exactly where you expect, and some are stitched in for a different reason.
puzzles.trap: The main misdirection is that several words read like straightforward fabric or sewing terms, but a few actually belong to wordplay groups instead.

puzzles.title: Field Work
puzzles.intro: Sixteen farm-flavored words are hiding four sets of four. Some of the most obvious-looking agricultural tiles are there to send you in the wrong direction.
puzzles.trap: The main feint is that several words seem to sort into straightforward farm buckets, but some actually belong to wordplay groups like ___ FIELD or terms with hidden grains.

puzzles.title: In the Press
puzzles.intro: Sixteen printing-adjacent words hide four different connections. Some will seem to point toward the page before they point toward the press.
puzzles.trap: I leaned on words like SCREEN, SCRIPT, and JACKET to suggest the wrong kind of print-related grouping before the more technical connections emerge.

puzzles.title: Orchard Tangles
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four groups. Since this one grows out of orchards, expect some fruitful wrong turns.
puzzles.trap: Several tiles look like they should sort by fruit first, but some are doing wordplay jobs instead — especially the ones nudging you toward trees and fruit anatomy.

puzzles.title: Shop Talk

groups.label: Lumber cuts sold at a yard

puzzles.intro: Sixteen shop-flavored words hide four sets. Some of the most carpenter-ish tiles actually belong to a wordplay group instead.
puzzles.trap: The main feint is that several words look interchangeable as tools or lumber terms, but some of them only lock in when you notice phrases with JOINT or alternate meanings of SAW.

puzzles.title: Volcanic Islands
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four hidden groups. Some island-looking entries belong somewhere much less geographic.
puzzles.trap: The main feint is that several place names suggest one big islands theme, but some actually belong to phrase-based categories instead.

puzzles.title: Cycle Tricks
puzzles.intro: Sixteen words, four hidden groups. Since this one’s built around cycling, expect a few terms to seem like they belong together before the real pattern emerges.
puzzles.trap: I loaded the grid with spinny-looking words and bike-adjacent terms so tiles like ROLL, TURN, BIKE, and CHAIN would tempt you into the wrong set first.

puzzles.title: Off the Map

groups.label: Hidden cardinal directions at the start

puzzles.intro: Sixteen tiles, four groups. Some cartographic terms are doing double duty, so don’t trust the first neat set you see.
puzzles.trap: The main feint is that several words look like they belong in straightforward map-terminology buckets, but some actually work better through wordplay and naming conventions.
